sub_answers.text: The Riga Football Cup was held intermittently between 1910 and 1936, indicating irregular staging of that national competition [d17125690s1p0]. The Latvian Football Union organized the Latvian Championship between 1922 and 1927 and it was replaced by Virsliga in 1927, indicating a change in championship structure and categories [d17125690s1p0].

sub_answers.text: Latvia lacked a primary national stadium for many years and relied on Daugava Stadium and Skonto Stadium for international games [d17125690s7p0]. Neither Daugava Stadium nor Skonto Stadium met UEFA/FIFA standards due to low seating capacity of less than 11,000 [d17125690s7p0]. Plans to build a modern stadium were put on hold because of unclear funding strategies among the UAE investors, the Latvian football governing body, and other organizations [d17125690s7p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Have there been criticisms or external assessments about the competitiveness or international relevance of Latvia's national championships?
sub_answers.text: Both Daugava Stadium and Skonto Stadium do not meet UEFA/FIFA standards, which limits their suitability for major international events [d17125690s7p0]. The Latvian Football Federation sought to build a modern 15,000–20,000-seat stadium to attract international events and improve relevance, reflecting concern about current international competitiveness of venues [d17125690s7p0].

sub_answers.text:
The classical 6.0 judging system was ended after a judging scandal at the 2002 Winter Olympics and replaced by the ISU Judging System beginning in 2004 [d4546369s3p0].
The 2003 Nebelhorn Trophy was the first international senior competition to use the ISU Judging System [d19361020s0p0].
Under the ISU Judging System, technical elements are assigned predetermined base point values and a panel of judges scores quality of execution with a Grade of Execution (GOE) from −5 to 5, with the panel GOE determined by a trimmed mean and added to the base value to generate each element's score [d73365603s7p0].
Under the ISU Judging System, performances are also scored on program components with judges assigning scores in 0.25 increments and the panel component scores determined by trimmed means, and deductions are applied for violations such as time infractions, stops, restarts, or falls before the final score is computed [d73365603s7p0].
